title.narrative: DRC Skills for Economic Transformation Project

description.narrative: The PDO is to increase the number of graduates with market-relevant skills and strengthen skills development systems for better and more inclusive jobs in priority sectors.

This proposed project takes a comprehensive, multisectoral approach to addressing skills development in the country. By tackling key barriers to quality, market-relevant training, the project seeks to modernize and professionalize curricula, strengthen infrastructure, and build meaningful partnerships with the private sector. It goes beyond traditional TVET and professional training to include higher education and informal apprenticeship systems, ensuring that no sector is left behind. To build a high-value-added, inclusive economy, there is a need to develop a diverse range of skills across the entire spectrum, engaging all key stakeholders, including those currently outside the system. Through an inter-ministerial approach, the project will develop targeted, scalable solutions to skill shortages and enhance employment prospects for all. The project will target six priority sectors: energy (including hydropower) and mining, transport and logistics, agriculture (agribusiness, livestock, and fisheries), manufacturing, tourism, and digital technology. Component 1: Increasing Equitable Access to Quality and Market-Relevant Skills for Youth (US$ 170.3 million). This component aims to improve access to essential TVET and skills development programs for youth, especially vulnerable and disadvantaged groups in targeted sectors. The component will modernize training delivery, strengthen pathways to employment and self-employment, and promote gender and social inclusion. - Subcomponent 1.1: Establish the Inga Academy of Excellence (US$ 30.3 million). This subcomponent will establish a flagship Center of Excellence in Kongo-Central to meet specialized workforce needs for the Inga hydropower program and related energy infrastructure. The Academy will modernize engineering programs and labs, build teaching capacity through regional and international collaboration for engineering students, university faculty, and researchers. - Subcomponent 1.2: Expand and Strengthen TVET Institutions and HEIs to Deliver Market-Relevant Skills (US$140 million). This subcomponent will extend support to select TVET institutions and HEIs that feed workforce needs for other strategic investments, including Lobito and the project six targeted priority sectors. Support will also target programs to strengthen country's capacity for advanced technical skills for large-scale infrastructure. Component 2: Enhancing Youth Employability and Productivity through Quality and Relevant Upskilling (US$ 70 M). This Component aims to improve youth employability, productivity, and income generation by supporting skills upgrading, entrepreneurship, and business development in key targeted sectors.- Subcomponent 2.1: Upgrading market-relevant skills and productivity for youth (US$20 million). This subcomponent aims to increase the productivity and earnings of young microentrepreneurs by upgrading their technical, business, and life skills, and supporting them to scale up their enterprises.- Subcomponent 2.2: Promoting Youth Entrepreneurship and Innovation through Competitive Fund (US$50 million). This subcomponent will support, and finance entrepreneurial initiatives (business plans) presented by the project beneficiaries who will be trained through the Competitive Fund. Component 3: Reinforcing Skills Systems through Harmonized Frameworks, Enhanced Digital Systems, and Project Management (US$60 million). This subcomponent aims at strengthening job market information, enhance data for evidence-based approaches to improving skills development, and support project management and monitoring and evaluation. - Sub-Component 3.1: Bridging and Harmonizing Skills Frameworks and Certification Systems (US$10 million). This subcomponent will focus on improving the coherence and recognition of skills development frameworks in DRC. - Subcomponent 3.2: Building Digital Systems for Labor Market Intelligence, and Project Management (US$50 million). This subcomponent will support the establishment of a statistical TVET database in the DRC; Technical and policy dialogue around the future demand for skills and; establishment of a countrywide skills strategy.
